Found by the 18.0 release QA sweep (subject `5b14b7f3`) while driving the item above; reproduced twice. Full run evidence: #24558.

## What is wrong

`plugin-audit` caches each object definition the first time it looks one up and never invalidates the cache (`audit-writers.ts`, `getObjectDef` → `objectDefCache`). An object whose `enable.files` is switched on through the metadata door keeps answering as if files were disabled for every attachment write until the server restarts. The metadata read-back already shows the new value, so nothing tells the author why the write is refused.

## Reproduction

1. Boot the showcase (`objectstack dev --seed-admin`), sign in as admin.
2. `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qa_kid` — a minimal object with no `enable` block → 200.
3. `POST /api/v1/data/sys_attachment` with `parent_object: "qa_kid"` (plus a parent id and file fields) → 403 `FILES_DISABLED` (correct at this point; this lookup populates the cache).
4. `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qa_kid` again with `enable: { files: true }` → 200; `GET /api/v1/meta/object/qa_kid` shows `enable.files: true`.
5. Repeat step 3 → expected: admitted; actual: still 403 `FILES_DISABLED`. Restarting the server makes the same request succeed.

Control: an object authored with `enable.files: true` from the start, and never looked up before, admits the attachment.

## Mechanism / fix direction

The cache needs invalidation on object metadata change (the ObjectQL registry already emits object-metadata events — the same channel other consumers subscribe to), or the lookup should resolve per call against the registry.

Severity: medium (functional; a runtime metadata change that silently does not take effect).
